explain.say: When a full moon happens near the closest point, called perigee, we get a supermoon. It looks about 14 percent wider and about 30 percent brighter than a full moon at the farthest point, called a micromoon.

faq.a: A supermoon is a full moon that happens when the Moon is near perigee, its closest point to Earth in its oval orbit. It looks slightly bigger and brighter than usual.

faq.q: How much bigger is a supermoon?
faq.a: Compared with a full moon at its farthest point, a supermoon looks about 14 percent wider and about 30 percent brighter. Compared with an average full moon, the difference is about half that.
asks: Can you tell a supermoon by eye?

faq.a: A micromoon is a full moon near apogee, the Moon's farthest point from Earth, about 406,000 kilometres away. It looks a little smaller and dimmer than usual.
asks: What is the opposite of a supermoon?

faq.q: Why does the Moon look huge near the horizon?
faq.a: That is a trick of the brain called the Moon illusion. A camera shows the rising Moon is the same size as when it is high in the sky; it only seems bigger beside trees and buildings.
asks: Is the Moon bigger when it rises?

faq.a: Yes, a little. A closer Moon pulls harder, so tides around a supermoon can be a few centimetres higher than usual, especially when they coincide with spring tides.

facts: The Moon's distance from Earth varies between about 356,000 and 407,000 kilometres.
A full moon near perigee appears about 14 percent wider and 30 percent brighter than one near apogee (NASA).
The word supermoon was coined by astrologer Richard Nolle in 1979.
